transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I came in because... I don't know, for a long time now I've just had this heavy, low feeling sitting on me. I mean, I still get through my driving routes and my volunteer shifts, but most days it feels like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like I'm not really present in my own life.
How long have you been experiencing this heavy, low feeling?
I'd say it's been going on for about three years now. It started right around the time my father died.
During these three years, have there been times—maybe weeks or months—when you felt notably better or when the heavy feeling lifted, or has it been pretty consistently there the whole time?

No, not really. I mean, I can't think of a time where it completely went away. It's just... it's just always there. Sometimes it's maybe a little easier to ignore when I'm busy on a route, but it hasn't ever really lifted. Not for a week, not for a month. It's just a constant thing.
Over these three years, have there been any periods—maybe lasting several days or a week or more—when you felt unusually energetic, very optimistic, or like you could do a lot more than usual?

No, uh, nothing like that. I haven't had any times where I felt super energetic or, you know, unusually optimistic. Like I said, it's just been that same steady, low feeling the whole time. I definitely haven't had any big bursts of energy where I felt like I could take on the world or anything.
During these three years, have there been any stretch of time—say two months or longer in a row—when you felt completely back to normal, with the heavy feeling gone?
No, definitely not. Like I was just saying, it hasn't even gone away for a single week. So, a whole two months? No. It's just been a steady weight this whole time.

I want to ask about sleep specifically. Over these three years, have you ever had a period—even just a few days—where you needed much less sleep than usual but still felt rested and energetic, like you could function fine on just 3 or 4 hours a night?

No, I've never had anything like that. I definitely need my sleep. If I don't get a full night, I'm just dragging the next day, especially driving the truck. So, no, I've never had a time where I felt fine on just a few hours of sleep.

Even though you've said the heavy feeling hasn't completely gone away, are there days or weeks when it feels a bit lighter or less intense than other times, or does it stay pretty much the same severity all the time?

Well, I mean, it's not always exactly the same every single day. Some days are maybe a little easier to get through than others, but... it never really goes away. It's always there in the background, even on the days that aren't quite as bad. So I guess it fluctuates a tiny bit, but mostly it just stays pretty steady.

You mentioned the heavy feeling fluctuates a tiny bit day to day, but I want to clarify: over these three years, have there been any stretches of time—say two months or longer—where your mood felt essentially normal, even if you weren't feeling great or energetic, just... normal and baseline?
No, I really haven't. Like I said earlier, it hasn't even gone away for a week. So, no, there hasn't been any two-month stretch where I felt normal or back to baseline. It's just always there.

Looking back over your whole life, not just these three years, have you ever had a stretch of time—say two years or more—where you felt persistently more upbeat, more confident, or more irritable than your baseline, even if you wouldn't call it 'high' or abnormal?

No, I can't say I have. I mean, before these last three years, I just felt... normal, I guess. Just regular. I never had any long stretches where I felt unusually upbeat or overly confident, or even extra irritable for years at a time. It was just an average, normal life before this heavy feeling set in.
Before these past three years, did you ever have a period in your life—maybe weeks or months at a time—when you felt this same kind of heavy, depressed mood that you're describing now?

No, not that I can remember. Like I said, before these last three years, things were just... normal. I mean, I'd have a bad day here and there, sure, everyone does. But nothing like this heavy feeling that just sticks around for months on end. I never really dealt with anything like this before it started three years ago.
Over these three years, have you noticed changes in your appetite, or do you find it harder to concentrate on things than you used to?

My appetite is pretty much the same, I haven't noticed much change there. But concentrating... yeah, it is a bit harder. 

I mean, I can still do my job fine, but lately I catch myself having to reread delivery times. Or I'll find myself just staring at the schedule board a lot longer than I really should. It's just like my mind doesn't lock onto things the way it used to.
